standard.title: Practise and perform informally
standard.description: practise and perform dances in informal settings
standard.prior_knowledge: Students have shared dance sequences in informal settings (Y1-2). They can present with expressive intent and reflect on performances using Viewpoints questions.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students practise and perform dances in informal settings.

nodes.label: Expressive skills in performance
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can use expressive skills — projection and focus — to communicate dance ideas to an audience.
nodes.minimum_width: Demonstrating at least one expressive skill (projection or focus) in a performance — student can name and describe what they are doing.
nodes.typical_width: Using expressive skills of projection and focus in informal performances: looking out and up to communicate joy; extending movements outwards; maintaining focus to communicate intention; practising these skills across multiple performances.
wider: Practise the same sequence with deliberate variation in expressive skill (e.g. with and without projection) — comparing what changes in the audience's experience
View recordings of own performances to identify where expressive skills are strong and where they could be developed

response_modes.reason: Expressive performance skills require repeated practice across many performance opportunities. Single performances don't build the consistency and confidence that genuine performance presence requires.

success_criteria: Student demonstrates projection or focus in their performance — visible to an observer
Student can name the expressive skill they are using and describe what it involves

nodes.label: Presenting and reflecting
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can present a dance to an audience, communicate its meaning and purpose, and be an attentive audience member for peers' work.
nodes.minimum_width: Performing one dance to the class; sharing the meaning and intended purpose in a class debrief; being attentive and providing at least one constructive feedback comment.
nodes.typical_width: Performing in informal class settings; using screen-based technologies or online platforms to present where appropriate; sharing meaning and purpose (own words, images, learnt terminology, movement, drawing); being an attentive audience and providing constructive feedback to peers.
wider: Present a dance on a digital platform (e.g. school learning management system) — adapting the introduction for a remote or asynchronous audience
Receive peer feedback on a performance and use it to make one specific revision — documenting the change and its effect
nodes.hinge_reason: Presenting and reflecting as a complete loop — performing, communicating intent, receiving feedback, reflecting — is the capability milestone of this standard. Students who have not closed this loop lack the reflective performance practice needed for the more formal and technically demanding presenting contexts of Y5-6.

response_modes.reason: Presenting integrates expressive skills (N1) with communicative intent and audience awareness. Debrief discussions are critical — 'What did you think my dance was about?' directly connects performance and reception.

success_criteria: Student performs a dance in an informal class setting using at least one expressive skill
Student can share the meaning or intended purpose of their dance using words, images or movement
Student provides at least one constructive, specific comment on a peer's performance
